title: The Usurper's Gambit
description: Ecktoria, heir to the shattered Utaran Empire, teeters on the edge of civil war. A charismatic pretender, Duke Logan the Bold, has won the militia's loyalty and begun invoking the ancient rites that would claim the Mandate of Everflame. The recognized heir, King Aldric the Lame, clings to power through law, tradition, and the blessing of a wavering High Temple. The party must move through marble forums, sealed archives, and a besieged basilica to decide who — if anyone — deserves the crown, in a city where legitimacy is manufactured as often as it is inherited.
author: Nicholas A. Gasper

bestiary.name: New Militia Enforcer
bestiary.description: A city militiaman who has traded the Lame King's grey sash for the Pretender's crimson one. Young, well-fed, and convinced reform is coming whether the old families like it or not. Fights in disciplined pairs, more comfortable clearing a colonnade of protesters than facing a real duel.

sb_spends.name: Whistle for Backup
sb_spends.effect: A second pair of enforcers arrives at the top of the next exchange.

sb_spends.name: Cordon the Street
sb_spends.effect: The enforcers seal an exit; escaping this scene now costs an additional action or a Sway/Subterfuge check DV 4.

bestiary.lore: Most of the New Militia are Ecktorian-born sons of merchants and guildsmen who were never welcome in the old Standard-Bearer companies. Logan gave them crimson sashes and back pay in arrears; that alone bought loyalty the Lame King never thought to offer.

bestiary.name: Veteran Standard-Bearer
bestiary.description: A grizzled loyalist of the old imperial legions, still carrying a genuine campaign standard rather than a militia sash. They fight with the patient discipline of soldiers who have buried three commanders and outlasted them all.

sb_spends.name: Hold the Line
sb_spends.effect: The Standard-Bearer and one ally gain +1 die to Body defense until the end of the exchange.

sb_spends.name: Rally Cry
sb_spends.effect: All Lame King loyalists in Near range clear 1 Fatigue and gain +1 die on their next Command roll.

bestiary.lore: These soldiers remember an empire that actually functioned. They are not fighting for Aldric the man so much as for the idea that law should outlast any single king's popularity.

acts.title: Act I — Cracks in Marble
acts.description: The party witnesses, firsthand, how fragile Ecktoria's legitimacy has become. Public ceremony and street theater are political weapons here, and the party must learn to read them before they can wield them.

scenes.title: The Envoy's Humiliation
scenes.description: Before the Great Baths of Aurix, the Lame King's Envoy is struck from their ceremonial staff and jeered by a crowd primed for the Pretender's heralds. The players arrive as witnesses, mediators, or bystanders swept into the spectacle — and their reaction here becomes the city's first read on where they stand.

timers.name: Legitimacy Timer
timers.description: Tracks how firmly public opinion and institutional weight have swung to the Pretender. Advances through the acts; when full, Logan controls the capital in all but name.

outcomes.clean: You defuse the humiliation before it becomes a riot; the Envoy is grateful and offers a name — Grand Magistrate Valeria Thorne — as someone worth speaking to.
outcomes.partial: The crowd disperses, but not before the story spreads with the worst details intact. Tick Legitimacy Timer +1.
outcomes.miss: The Envoy is struck again, publicly, in front of you. Tick Legitimacy Timer +2 and the party is marked as bystanders who did nothing.

outcomes.clean: You recognize planted agitators among the jeering crowd — this humiliation was staged, not spontaneous.
outcomes.partial: You sense something's off but can't place it without more digging.
outcomes.miss: You misjudge the mood entirely and are swept along with the crowd's momentum.

scenes.title: Statues and Sashes
scenes.description: Overnight, imperial statues along the Forum colonnade have had their sashes repainted crimson, and militia in unfamiliar colors now stand where grey-sashed Standard-Bearers once did. The change is subtle enough to deny, obvious enough to unsettle anyone who's lived here more than a season.

outcomes.clean: You trace the paint to a guild workshop paid in advance by a New Merchant sympathetic to Logan — hard evidence of coordinated messaging.
outcomes.partial: You confirm the change is deliberate, but the trail to who ordered it goes cold at a middleman.
outcomes.miss: You're seen investigating by New Militia and questioned; nothing incriminating, but you're now a face they remember.

outcomes.clean: You talk your way past or subdue them without incident; word doesn't spread.
outcomes.partial: The encounter ends without violence, but the militia file a report noting your names and business.
outcomes.miss: Things turn physical. Tick Legitimacy Timer +1 as the militia spin the story as an attack on lawful order.

outcomes.clean: You collect three solid leads: Duke Logan's coronation rite is already being drafted at the Coin-House; Grand Magistrate Thorne has gone quiet; a courier died carrying a sealed tablet last week.
outcomes.partial: You get rumor and noise, mostly contradictory, but confirm the political temperature is rising fast.
outcomes.miss: You draw attention from Silent Opposition watchers who now know outsiders are asking questions.

acts.title: Act II — Shadows in the Censorium
acts.description: Grand Magistrate Valeria Thorne, keeper of every precedent that governs imperial succession, is attacked in her own hall. The party must decide how far they're willing to go into Ecktoria's archive of buried truths to learn who actually has the stronger claim — and discover that the answer is messier than either faction wants it to be.

scenes.title: The Magistrate's Hall
scenes.description: Thorne is found bleeding on the floor of her own study, files scattered, a censer overturned. She survives, but she's frightened in a way that unsettles everyone who knows her reputation for icy composure. Someone wanted a specific document before she could act on it.

timers.name: Legal Standing — Aldric
timers.description: Tracks the strength of the Lame King's documented legal claim. Advances when the party surfaces genuine precedent or legitimate support for him.

timers.name: Legal Standing — Logan
timers.description: Tracks the strength of the Pretender's claim. Advances when the party surfaces genuine precedent or legitimate support for him.

outcomes.clean: Thorne tells you what was taken: a genealogical record referencing 'the Pact of Three Flames' and a name she won't speak aloud yet. Tick Legal Standing — Aldric +1.
outcomes.partial: She's too shaken to say more than 'the Censor's Hall — go now.' You have a destination but no context.
outcomes.miss: She loses consciousness before saying anything useful, and the attending priest orders you out.

outcomes.clean: You catch the fleeing agent — not militia, not a soldier, but a Censor's Hall clerk paid by the Silent Opposition to muddy both claims equally.
outcomes.partial: You lose them in the crowd but recover a dropped token marking them as Censor's Hall staff.
outcomes.miss: You lose the trail entirely and alert whoever hired them that someone's watching.

scenes.title: The Censor's Hall
scenes.description: A labyrinth of red-lacquered tablets and censored histories, where the Line of Fire — the genealogical record of every legitimate claimant in a century — is kept under lock the party does not have.

outcomes.clean: You reach the Line of Fire unnoticed and have time to actually read it before anyone comes looking.
outcomes.partial: You get in, but a night clerk notices something's disturbed and raises a quiet alarm — you have limited time before guards arrive.
outcomes.miss: You're caught red-handed. Tick Legitimacy Timer +1 as word spreads that outsiders were rifling the imperial archive.

outcomes.clean: The truth is uncomfortable for everyone: Aldric's line is legitimate but was formalized through a procedural shortcut two generations back that Logan's lawyers could plausibly challenge — and Logan's own bloodline claim is real, but far more distant than his heralds claim. Both sides have been telling half-truths. Gain the 'Pact of Three Flames' clause, usable as leverage on either faction.
outcomes.partial: You confirm one side's claim is shakier than advertised but can't yet prove which, or resolve the ambiguity cleanly.
outcomes.miss: You misread the censored annotations and walk away with a plausible-sounding but wrong conclusion — which could be dangerous if you act on it.

acts.title: Act III — Coin, Steel, and Fire
acts.description: The Pretender's forces blockade the Fire-Blessed Basilica, where any coronation must ultimately be sanctified. The party's information and alliances from the first two acts now become leverage — or liabilities — as every faction moves to lock in its position before the crisis resolves itself without them.

scenes.title: The Coin-House Floor
scenes.description: Ecktoria's financial temple, where abacus-boards and chanting clerks quietly decide which faction can actually afford to win. Sabotaging or securing this support here shapes the Coronation Readiness Timer more than any speech in the Forum.

timers.name: Coronation Readiness Timer
timers.description: Tracks how prepared Logan's coronation bid is to proceed. Advances as his faction secures funding, military support, and public opinion.

outcomes.clean: You redirect or expose a major funding stream, decisively shifting financial backing toward whichever faction you support. Advance or retreat Coronation Readiness Timer by 2, GM's choice matching your action.
outcomes.partial: You cause a disruption, but the clerks quietly route around it within the day.
outcomes.miss: You're identified interfering with sealed financial records — a crime that carries real legal weight in Ecktoria. Tick Legitimacy Timer +1 against you specifically.

outcomes.clean: The merchant guilds commit real resources to your chosen side — or agree to withhold support from both, buying the party room to maneuver.
outcomes.partial: They'll help, but want something concrete in return — a favor, a contract, a promise the party may regret making.
outcomes.miss: They read the party as unreliable and quietly begin hedging against them specifically.

scenes.title: The Basilica Blockade
scenes.description: Logan's militia rings the Fire-Blessed Basilica, ostensibly for 'public safety' ahead of a coronation that hasn't been sanctified yet. High Priest Dominicus is trapped inside with the Sacred Brazier, torn between the stability of tradition and the pull of a renewal he isn't certain is genuine.

outcomes.clean: You get inside, or get a channel of communication open, without a full battle in the street.
outcomes.partial: You get through, but it costs — a Standard-Bearer or Militia unit is hurt on your account, and the political blame will land on someone.
outcomes.miss: The blockade holds and the confrontation escalates publicly. Tick Legitimacy Timer +2.

outcomes.clean: Dominicus commits to a position — conditional blessing pending proof of legitimate succession, refusing to be rushed by either faction. This effectively freezes any coronation until the party resolves the succession question honestly.
outcomes.partial: He remains publicly neutral but privately leans toward whichever side seems most sincere, not most powerful — a soft advantage the party can build on.
outcomes.miss: He caves to the pressure of the blockade itself and prepares to bless whoever controls the building when the ritual hour comes — meaning force, not legitimacy, may decide everything.

acts.title: Act IV — The Coronation of Ash or Glory
acts.description: Dawn breaks over the Basilica. Every thread the party has pulled — legal, financial, religious, popular — converges into a single ritual hour. This is not a fight to be won by force alone; it is a public reckoning over what legitimacy actually means in a dying empire.

scenes.title: The Reckoning at the Basilica
scenes.description: Aldric, Logan, and whatever third option the party has built all converge at the Basilica steps as the Coronation Readiness Timer and Legal Standing timers reach their conclusions. Dominicus waits at the Sacred Brazier, and the crowd — real people, not a mechanic — watches to see who blinks first.

outcomes.clean: The party's evidence and alliances carry the day publicly — whichever outcome they've built toward becomes the crowd's outcome too, not just the factions'.
outcomes.partial: The crowd is swayed but divided; the resolution holds, but resentment and rival claims will linger for years.
outcomes.miss: The debate collapses into shouting and the decision falls to whoever has soldiers in the square, not whoever has the truth.

outcomes.clean: Dominicus blesses the outcome the party has built the strongest legitimate case for, whether that's Aldric, Logan, or a third path — and the Everflame's sanction quiets most dissent.
outcomes.partial: Dominicus blesses an outcome, but publicly notes his reservations, ensuring the winner's legitimacy is real but not unquestioned.
outcomes.miss: Dominicus refuses to bless anyone until the succession dispute is resolved through proper channels — postponing the crisis, not solving it, and leaving the city in dangerous limbo.

npcs.name: King Aldric the Lame
npcs.motivation: Preserve legitimate succession and imperial stability, even if it means the empire changes only glacially.
npcs.secret: He knows his own claim was formalized through a procedural shortcut two generations back. He has spent his reign making sure no one looks closely enough to find it — which is why he's slower to challenge Logan's claim than his advisors want.

npcs.name: Duke Logan the Bold
npcs.motivation: Seize power through popular support and promise of reform, genuinely believing the empire needs him more than it needs the old rules.
npcs.secret: His bloodline claim is real but far more distant than his heralds advertise — several generations more distant than any prior claimant has attempted to press. He knows this, and knows that if the Line of Fire is read too carefully, his 'restoration' looks a great deal more like a coup.

npcs.name: Grand Magistrate Valeria Thorne
npcs.role: Keeper of imperial law and succession precedent
npcs.motivation: Preserve the legal integrity of the imperial system, even when the law itself is inconvenient for everyone including her.
npcs.secret: She has known about the flaw in Aldric's formalization for years and buried it out of personal loyalty to his late father. The attack on her wasn't random — someone else found out she knew, and wanted to make sure she never had to choose between the law and her conscience.

npcs.name: High Priest Dominicus
npcs.role: Keeper of the Sacred Brazier and the Everflame
npcs.motivation: Ensure whoever receives divine sanction actually deserves it — stability matters to him, but not more than honesty.
npcs.secret: He has already privately decided he will not bless a coronation built on force or fear, regardless of which faction wins the street. He is waiting to see who brings him truth instead of an army.

npcs.name: The Lame King's Envoy
npcs.motivation: Advance Aldric's cause through means the king himself cannot be seen using.
npcs.secret: The Envoy is not acting purely on Aldric's orders — they are also quietly investigating whether Aldric's own claim will survive scrutiny, because if it won't, they intend to have a contingency ready before anyone else finds out.

locations.name: The Grand Forum
locations.description: A marble theater of politics with multi-level balconies, statues of emperors, and mosaic floors that carry political messages as loudly as any speech. Public opinion lives and dies here.

locations.name: Imperial Arena
locations.description: Site of trials by ordeal and ceremonial oaths, riddled with underground tunnels and heavily guarded during public events.

locations.name: Coin-House Floor
locations.description: A Byzantine-style financial temple of abacus-boards and wax tablets, where clerks chant transactions that can bankrupt provinces or fund armies.

locations.name: Censor's Hall
locations.description: A labyrinth of red-lacquered tablets, genealogical records, and censored histories. Access requires high-level authorization the party almost certainly doesn't have.

locations.name: The Fire-Blessed Basilica
locations.description: The spiritual heart of Ecktoria, its gold-and-lapis dome depicting the Everflame. Any coronation must be sanctified here. Currently blockaded by the Pretender's forces.

factions.name: The Lame King's Line
factions.goals: Preserve law and tradition through Aldric's succession; strengths in ritual and institutional authority, weakness in speed and popular appeal.
factions.relationship: Controlled but slipping toward Desperate as public support erodes. DV for alliance: 4 (mutual benefit), 5 (neutral), 6+ (opposed).

factions.name: The Pretender's Cause
factions.goals: Install Logan through the 'New Augustan Revival,' leveraging popular support, military flexibility, and economic pressure over legal standing.
factions.relationship: Currently Dominant through popular momentum but shallow on legal legitimacy. DV for alliance: 3 (shared goals), 4 (neutral), 5+ (opposed).

factions.name: The Silent Opposition
factions.goals: Reject both claimants and secure provincial autonomy through economic sabotage and covert manipulation.
factions.relationship: Hidden and Controlled, patient rather than powerful. DV for alliance: 4 (shared opposition), 5 (neutral), 6+ (competing interests).

campaignTimers.name: Legitimacy Timer
campaignTimers.description: Tracks the drift of public and institutional opinion toward the Pretender. When full, Logan achieves effective control of the capital regardless of the legal question.

campaignTimers.name: Legal Standing — Aldric
campaignTimers.description: Strength of Aldric's documented legal claim. When full, his claim is unimpeachable in Ecktorian courts.

campaignTimers.name: Legal Standing — Logan
campaignTimers.description: Strength of Logan's documented legal claim. When full, his claim is unimpeachable in Ecktorian courts.

campaignTimers.name: Coronation Readiness Timer
campaignTimers.description: How prepared Logan's faction is to force a coronation regardless of legal resolution. When full, the coronation proceeds by force of arms.

notes: This adventure runs on parallel timers rather than a single villain clock — the party should feel like every faction is a legitimate, if flawed, political actor, not a shorthand for good or evil. The twist (both claims have real flaws) should surface gradually through Act II investigation, not be dumped in one exposition scene. The strongest endings come from players building a genuinely defensible third path rather than simply picking a winner. Designed for 4-5 sessions; can compress to 3 by combining Acts I and II if the table wants a faster pace.

pacing.act1: Establish Ecktoria as a place where ceremony IS politics — every gesture, sash color, and mosaic panel is a move on the board. Let the party witness the Envoy's humiliation as bystanders first; their reaction (intervene, investigate, or stay neutral) sets their initial reputation with both factions. Don't rush to reveal that both claims are flawed — that's an Act II discovery, earned through the archive, not handed out here.
pacing.act2: This act is the emotional and legal core of the adventure. Thorne's attack should feel personal and frightening, not just a plot device — she is one of the few characters in Ecktoria who has chosen truth over comfort, and it's cost her. The genealogical puzzle (verifying claimant lineages) is the mechanical centerpiece: both Aldric's and Logan's claims should turn out to be real but compromised, in different ways, so that neither faction is simply 'right.' Resist the urge to make this a shocking betrayal reveal — it should read as the natural, sad consequence of an empire that has been quietly cutting legal corners for generations.
pacing.act3: Coin, Steel, and Fire is about consequences catching up. Every relationship or piece of leverage from Acts I-II should matter here — track who owes the party what. The Coin-House and Basilica scenes should run in whatever order the table wants; don't force sequence. Dominicus's storyline (torn between stability and renewal) should culminate in him refusing to be rushed, which raises the stakes for Act IV rather than resolving them early.
pacing.act4: The coronation should feel like a genuine public reckoning, not a boss fight. If the party has built a strong case (legal, financial, religious, or popular), let mechanics reflect that they've already effectively won before the final rolls — the encounters here are about whether the city as a whole accepts that victory, not whether the party can out-fight anyone. Reward creative third-path solutions generously; that's the ending this adventure is built to reward.

npcSecrets.king-aldric: His claim's procedural flaw should never be presented as fraud — it was a shortcut taken during a genuine crisis two generations ago, the kind of thing that happens in every long-lived bureaucracy. His caution about pressing Logan too hard on legitimacy comes from fear of exactly this scrutiny being turned back on him.
npcSecrets.duke-logan: Logan genuinely believes his own cause, which is what makes him dangerous and sympathetic rather than a simple villain. His heralds have been rounding up his bloodline claim for years; he's aware of this but has let it happen because he believes the empire needs him regardless of the technicalities.
npcSecrets.grand-magistrate-thorne: She is the moral center of the adventure — a woman who has spent years balancing personal loyalty against professional integrity, and is finally being forced to choose. Her attack should read as a consequence of that choice becoming known, not a random act of violence.
npcSecrets.high-priest-dominicus: He has already made up his mind that force and fear cannot substitute for legitimacy, but he keeps this private until Act IV to preserve his position as a genuinely neutral arbiter — announcing it early would make him a target for both factions immediately.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: That both Aldric's and Logan's claims have real legal flaws — this is the Act II archive discovery; don't foreshadow it as a 'twist,' let it emerge as the natural texture of imperial bureaucracy
The specific nature of Thorne's knowledge about Aldric's formalization — she should stay evasive and frightened until the party has earned real trust or found independent evidence
Dominicus's private decision to reject force-based coronation — reveal only in Act IV, when it becomes the fulcrum of the climax
That the Silent Opposition orchestrated the attack on Thorne — this should surface through investigation (the captured clerk in Act II), not be stated outright

tacticalHints.legitimacy_vs_force: Constantly remind players that military and financial power are not the same as legitimacy in Ecktoria — a faction can be Dominant in the streets and still lose at the Basilica if the party builds a strong enough legal and religious case against them.
tacticalHints.third_path_support: If players start angling toward a third path (hidden claimant, Council of Three Flames, regional autonomy), lean in — provide NPC reactions (Thorne cautiously approving, Dominicus intrigued, both factions alarmed) that make it feel viable rather than punishing improvisation.
tacticalHints.timer_visibility: Make the Legitimacy and Legal Standing timers visible in play — describe crowds thickening, militia colors spreading, or archive dust settling differently as they shift, so the table feels the drift even between sessions.
